**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/02/15 (Wed) 20:59
- [USER] The user is a small or medium privately owned business owner.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Employee Retention Credit (ERC) is a tax credit designed to encourage businesses to keep their employees on payroll during difficult economic times, including the COVID-19 pandemic.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The ERC is available to eligible employers who experienced a significant decline in gross receipts or were partially or fully suspended due to government orders related to COVID-19.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The ERC is a refundable tax credit, meaning eligible employers can receive a refund if the credit exceeds their tax liability.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The credit is equal to 70% of qualified wages paid to each eligible employee, up to a maximum of $10,000 per employee per quarter.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The maximum credit per employee is $28,000 for 2021.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] To be eligible for the ERC, an employer must have experienced a significant decline in gross receipts or been partially or fully suspended due to government orders related to COVID-19.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The decline in gross receipts must be at least 20% in 2021 compared to the same quarter in 2019.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Small or medium privately owned businesses can benefit greatly from the ERC.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The credit can help offset the cost of keeping employees on payroll during difficult economic times.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] To claim the ERC, eligible employers must file Form 941, Employer's Quarterly Federal Tax Return, with the IRS.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] It is recommended that business owners consult with a tax professional to determine their eligibility and the amount of credit they may be eligible to receive.
